t: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for the procurement of or for the payment of the salary of any person engaged in the procurement of any hand or measuring tool(s) not produced in the United States or its possessions except to the extent that the Administrator of General Services or his designee shall determine that a satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity of hand or measuring tools produced in the United States or its possessions cannot be procured as and when needed from sources in the United States and its possessions or except in accordance with procedures prescribed by section 6–104.4(b) of Armed Services Procurement Regulation dated January 1, 1969, as such regulation existed on June 15, 1970. This section shall be applicable to all solicitations for bids opened after its enactment.

fable.w: This is an appropriations restriction on buying foreign-made hand or measuring tools, with an exception that turns on a determination made solely by a federal official, the Administrator of General Services. The tempting reading is that the reference to the Armed Services Procurement Regulation or to solicitations for bids signals rulemaking or outside involvement. That fails because the section only cites an already existing regulation rather than authorizing new rulemaking, and bidding on contracts is not participation in a federal decision. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: except to the extent that the Administrator of General Services or his designee shall determine that a satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity of hand or measuring tools produced in the United States or its possessions cannot be procured

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a restriction on federal appropriations for procuring tools, requiring that they be produced in the United States unless the Administrator of General Services determines otherwise. The decision-making process described involves only federal officials (the Administrator of General Services) and references internal procurement regulations. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for the procurement of or for the payment of the salary of any person engaged in the procurement of any hand or measuring tool(s) not produced in the United States or its possessions except to the extent that the Administrator of General Services or his designee shall determine that a satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity of hand or measuring tools produced in the United States or its possessions cannot be procured as and when needed from sources in the United States and its possessions or except in accordance with procedures prescribed by section 6–104.4(b) of Armed Services Procurement Regulation dated January 1, 1969, as such regulation existed on June 15, 1970.

opus.w: This is a Buy-American funding restriction. The only exception depends on a decision by a federal official (the GSA Administrator or his designee), and that decision involves no consultation, hearing, or advisory body with outside parties. The tempting readings fail: the procurement-regulation reference points to an existing rule frozen as of 1970 rather than new rulemaking authority, and solicitations for bids are contract applications, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: except to the extent that the Administrator of General Services or his designee shall determine that a satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity of hand or measuring tools produced in the United States or its possessions cannot be procured as and when needed
opus.b:
**Step 1 — Reasoning.** It's tempting to read "procedures prescribed by section 6–104.4(b) of Armed Services Procurement Regulation" or "solicitations for bids" as participation. Neither holds up. The regulation reference points to a rule that already existed on a fixed past date (June 15, 1970). It doesn't give anyone new authority to make rules. Bids are contract solicitations, which the definition excludes as applications. The only decision-maker is the Administrator of General Services, a federal official, and nobody outside the government is consulted.

**Step 2 — Answer.**

qwen_chat.w: This section restricts the use of federal funds for procuring non-domestic tools unless the Administrator of General Services determines that domestic tools are unavailable. This determination is made by a federal official internally. There is no requirement for consultation with outside parties, public comment, or an advisory board with non-federal members. The reference to procurement regulations does not itself constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for the procurement of or for the payment of the salary of any person engaged in the procurement of any hand or measuring tool(s) not produced in the United States or its possessions except to the extent that the Administrator of General Services or his designee shall determine that a satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity of hand or measuring tools produced in the United States or its possessions cannot be procured as and when needed from sources in the United States and its possessions
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to "procedures prescribed by section 6–104.4(b) of Armed Services Procurement Regulation" implies a process involving outside parties (e.g., bidders). However, the section itself does not describe those procedures, nor does it mandate any specific interaction with outside parties. It merely sets a restriction on the use of funds based on a determination by a federal official (the Administrator of General Services). The determination is made internally by the federal government. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with states/tribes, or an advisory board with non-federal members in this specific text.
